key_insight: Separating agent skills into Meta, Experience, Tool, and Script components enables more effective skill evolution than treating each skill as a single artifact.
engineering_relevance: Agent developers can use function-specific updates, validation, and adaptive invocation to maintain reusable capabilities learned from execution trajectories.
method: Extract evidence-grounded semantic gradients from successful and failed trajectories.
Consolidate learning signals by functional role and apply component-specific updates and validation.
Coordinate components and adaptively invoke them during task execution.
evidence_signal: CDSE ranked highest in all 36 settings spanning six benchmarks, three agent models, and two execution harnesses, averaging gains of 7.6 percentage points over Base and 2.6 over the strongest competitor per setting.
watch_item: Component-specific maintenance and cross-component coordination may add implementation overhead; the abstract does not quantify runtime or cost.
paper_title: From Trajectories to Differentiated Skills: Cognitive Differentiation for Self-Improving Agents
